headlines.text: On a Saturday in 2025, back when the AEW World Heavyweight Title had a new owner by the end of the night as MJF vs. Adam Page vs. Samoa Joe vs. Swerve Strickland battled it out, appearing on Worlds End, rated 7.37 ? a solid showing ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. It was the 70th time the AEW World Heavyweight Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. MJF cashed in his Casino Gauntlet contract, capitalizing on a low blow to Adam Page to pin Samoa Joe and reclaim the AEW World Championship in a four-way also involving Swerve Strickland.

It was 2023 when Eddie Kingston vs. Bryan Danielson met in a Continental Classic Semi-Final on Dynamite, rated 8.70 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype, part of the special New Year's Smash '23 - Night 1 card.
On this day in 2024, Hook vs. Nick Wayne crossed paths for the first time ever, in the night's main event on Rampage, rated 6.12.

secondaries.text: It was 2025 when a new champion was crowned for the AEW Continental Title as Jon Moxley vs. Kazuchika Okada battled it out, appearing on Worlds End, rated 6.98 ? ending the champion's reign at 13 defenses. In their first-ever meeting, Moxley defeated Kazuchika Okada in the Continental Classic final, ending Okada's 647-day reign and winning his first-ever C2 tournament.

That Saturday in 2025, Jon Moxley vs. Kyle Fletcher met in a Continental Classic Semi-Final on Worlds End, rated 9.36 ? one of the greatest matches in company history ? part of a stacked Worlds End '25 card, rated 8.02 overall. Fletcher competed in the loaded Worlds End undercard as the Continental Classic and World Title storylines collided around him.

Flash back to 2025, when Babes Of Wrath vs. Athena & Mone went to battle over the AEW Women's World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Worlds End, rated 6.67. Athena & Mone was challenging for gold for the very first time.
